# BrowserDJ

> A music studio that runs entirely in the browser (piano roll, drum sequencer, playlist, mixer, WAV and MIDI export). No accounts, no server, nothing uploaded.

AI agents are welcome to make songs here. If you can run JavaScript in the page (a browser agent, devtools, or a
headless browser), the page has a small, stable interface for composing while the person watches it appear:

    BrowserDJ.agent.help()     // the full reference, with the real instrument, kit and drum names

Each call is one undo step and shows what it did in the status line. Bars count from 1; inside a pattern, times are
beats (4 per bar). Pitches are MIDI numbers or names ('C4' = 60). Mistakes throw a message that says what is allowed,
and change nothing.

You cannot hear the result, so `await BrowserDJ.agent.listen()` renders the song offline and returns numbers:
loudness per marked section, peak, loudness per second, and warnings (clipping, silence). `check()` points out
notes outside the key and patterns that are not placed. `await shareLink()` gives a link that opens the song for anyone.

## A first song

    const a = BrowserDJ.agent;
    a.newSong({name: 'First try', bpm: 100, key: 'A', scale: 'minor'});   // replaces the open song (Undo brings it back)
    const keys = a.addTrack({instrument: 'ep', name: 'Keys', reverb: 0.3});
    const k = a.addPattern(keys, {name: 'Chords', notes: a.chords('Am F C G').flatMap((c, i) => c.map((p) => [p + 12, i * 4, 4, 80]))});
    const d = a.addTrack({type: 'drums', kit: 'acoustic'});
    const beat = a.addPattern(d, {steps: {kick: 'x.......x.x.....', snare: '....x.......x...', chat: 'x.x.x.x.x.x.x.x.'}});
    a.addClip(k, 1, 8); a.addClip(beat, 5, 4);
    a.addMarker(1, 'Intro'); a.addMarker(5, 'Groove');
    console.log(await a.listen());

## Calls

- Song: newSong, setSong, info, summary, song (the project as JSON), load
- Tracks: addTrack, setTrack, removeTrack
- Patterns: addPattern, setPattern (notes for synths; step strings like 'x... o... x... o...' for drums, with optional chance rows)
- Arrangement: addClip, clearClips, addMarker, automate
- Helpers: chord, chords, scale, note, noteName
- Ears and hands: check, listen, play, stop, undo, shareLink

## Without running code

A song is a JSON file (`*.browserdj.json`). The examples (https://github.com/pvdptje/BrowserDJ/tree/master/examples) are
made by small Node scripts in `tools/make-*.js`, which are good models. Drop a .browserdj.json or .mid file onto the page to open it.
